title: Notes on d-matching polynomials, gcd-matrix permanents, and partition self-divisibility, with Lean 4 formalizations
description: Four notes in combinatorics and number theory, with a methodology note, by Vico Bonfioli, each paired with a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization. The Lean library builds with no sorry, and every mathematical theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms; native_decide appears only where the kernel provably cannot evaluate, and the inferences drawn from those computed values are separately kernel-checked. (1) Roots of d-matching polynomials and the spectrum of the universal cover. Hall-Puder-Sawin place the roots of mu_{d,G} in an interval; we conjecture they lie in the spectrum of the universal cover itself, which is the matching-polynomial form of their Question 6.3 and contains Problem 1 of Song-Fan-Miao. Proved for every graph of first Betti number one and every d, via a closed form which for the cycle specializes to an independent proof of Hall's conjecture; and proved for every subdivision at d=1. In operator form we give a vertex recursion for weighted 2-plane families valid in every direction, whose leading cross term is shown to be a perfect square, and identify the cavity ratio at the threshold exactly. The band itself is open, reduced to the sign of a single quantity. (2) The permanent of the gcd matrix a(n)=per[gcd(i,j)] (OEIS A085244): a family of congruences, v2(a(n)) tending to infinity, and (a(n)/n!)^(1/n) tending to infinity unconditionally. The 2-adic deficit at the peaks n=2^k+1 is explained through a mechanism, for the weight-zero grade of a(n); transfer to a(n) itself is verified only for small k and is not claimed in general. Whether the governing parity is odd infinitely often is open. (3) Coefficient stability of d-matching polynomials, with the coefficient extraction, the inclusion-exclusion and the cover counts all machine-checked. (4) Integers n with n dividing p(n)-1, over Mathlib's combinatorial partition function. Conjectures are labelled as such throughout, and the formalization scope of each result is stated where the result appears.
